answer:
The given system of linear equations can be written in matrix form $AX = B$:
$$\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 5 & 6 & 7 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha \\ \beta \\ \gamma \end{bmatrix}$$

Consider the augmented matrix $[A|B]$:
$$[A|B] = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 5 & \alpha \\ 4 & 5 & 6 & \beta \\ 5 & 6 & 7 & \gamma \end{bmatrix}$$

Apply row operations to reduce to row echelon form:
$R_2 \to 3R_2 - 4R_1$ and $R_3 \to 3R_3 - 5R_1$:
$$\sim \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 5 & \alpha \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 3\beta - 4\alpha \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 3\gamma - 5\alpha \end{bmatrix}$$

Apply $R_3 \to R_3 - 2R_2$:
$$\sim \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 5 & \alpha \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 3\beta - 4\alpha \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & (3\gamma - 5\alpha) - 2(3\beta - 4\alpha) \end{bmatrix}$$

Simplifying the last element of the augmented column:
$$3\gamma - 5\alpha - 6\beta + 8\alpha = 3\alpha - 6\beta + 3\gamma = 3(\alpha - 2\beta + \gamma)$$

For the system to be consistent, the rank of $A$ must equal the rank of $[A|B]$. Since the third row of $A$ becomes all zeros, the corresponding element in the augmented matrix must also be zero:
$$3(\alpha - 2\beta + \gamma) = 0 \implies \alpha - 2\beta + \gamma = 0 \implies \beta - \alpha = \gamma - \beta$$

This condition implies that $\alpha, \beta,$ and $\gamma$ are in Arithmetic Progression (A.P.). Hence proved.
proTip: When checking consistency using parameters, apply row operations until the bottom row of coefficient matrix becomes zero, then equate the augmented part to zero.
